events.title: Rome founded
events.detail:
Rome founded

According to legend, Romulus founded the city on the Palatine Hill after killing his twin brother Remus.

events.title: Republic begins
events.detail:
The Republic begins

The last king, Tarquin the Proud, is expelled and power passes to two elected consuls.

events.title: Battle of Marathon
events.detail:
Battle of Marathon

Athens defeats the first Persian invasion.

events.title: First Punic War
events.detail:
First Punic War

Rome fights Carthage over Sicily and builds its first large navy.

events.title: War with Rome
events.detail:
War with Rome

Carthage, the dominant naval power of the western Mediterranean, is drawn into war over Sicily.

events.title: Cannae
events.detail:
Battle of Cannae

Hannibal encircles and destroys a much larger Roman army.

events.title: Carthage and Corinth destroyed
events.detail:
-146

Carthage and Corinth destroyed

Rome razes Carthage at the end of the Third Punic War and crushes the Achaean League in Greece, becoming master of the Mediterranean.

events.title: Caesar crosses the Rubicon
events.detail:
Crossing the Rubicon

Julius Caesar leads his army into Italy, starting a civil war.

events.title: Caesar assassinated
events.detail:
Ides of March

Caesar is stabbed by a group of senators led by Brutus and Cassius.

events.title: Augustus becomes emperor
events.detail:
-27

Augustus becomes emperor

Octavian receives the title Augustus, ending the Republic and starting the Roman Empire and the Pax Romana.

events.title: Colosseum opens
events.detail:
The Colosseum

Opened under Titus with 100 days of games.

events.title: Maximum extent
events.detail:
Maximum extent

Under Trajan the empire reaches its largest size.

events.title: Empire splits
events.detail:
The empire splits

The eastern half, with Greek as its main language, continues as the Byzantine Empire.

events.title: Western Empire falls
events.detail:
Fall of the Western Empire

Odoacer deposes the last western emperor, Romulus Augustulus.
